learning.learning_goal: Understand a fraction by naming the whole, the equal-part size, and how many parts are present.
learning.big_idea: A fraction is one number whose value depends on a chosen whole divided into equal parts.
novice_success_criteria: explain what the denominator and numerator mean
compare fractions using part size rather than digit size

screens.label: Lesson 006 · Prototype
screens.title: What do the two numbers in a fraction mean?
screens.body: A fraction names equal-sized parts of a chosen whole. The whole must be clear before the fraction can be interpreted.
screens.callout: No fraction vocabulary is assumed. We will define each number from the model.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Does the larger bottom number make a larger piece?
screens.prompt: The same-size board is cut into 4 equal parts and another into 8 equal parts. Which single piece is larger?

choices.text: One fourth, because dividing the same whole into fewer parts makes each part larger
choices.feedback: With the same whole, 4 equal parts are larger than 8 equal parts because fewer cuts make larger pieces.

choices.text: One eighth, because 8 is larger than 4
They must match because both are one piece

hints: Imagine cutting the same board only 4 times versus 8 times.
The bottom number describes how many equal parts make one whole.

screens.label: Observe
screens.title: Keep the whole fixed and make 4 equal parts.

visual.ariaLabel: One whole bar divided into four equal parts with three parts filled
visual.message: The whole is divided into 4 equal-size parts; 3 are selected.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: What does 3/4 describe?

visual.ariaLabel: A bar showing three of four equal parts
visual.message: The 4 determines each part's size. The 3 counts those parts.

choices.text: Three parts, each sized as one fourth of the same whole
choices.feedback: The denominator defines the equal-part unit; the numerator counts copies of that unit.

choices.text: The unrelated whole numbers 3 and 4
Three pieces of any size

hints: First name the same whole shown by the entire bar.
Every selected piece must be one of 4 equal parts.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Give each number a precise job.

visual.ariaLabel: Three selected parts from a whole divided into four equal parts
visual.message: Read 3/4 as three copies of the unit one fourth.

definitions.meaning: the number of equal parts in one whole; it determines part size
the number of those equal-sized parts being counted

screens.guidance: Do not interpret either number until the whole and equal parts are identified.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Name the whole. Size the parts. Count the parts.
screens.hook: Denominator defines the part size; numerator counts copies of that part.
screens.body: The two numbers work together to name one value.
rebuildSteps: Use the denominator to divide it into equal parts.
Use the numerator to count copies of that part.
Locate the value relative to 0, 1, and beyond 1.
screens.boundary: “Bottom splits, top counts” is incomplete unless the whole, equality of parts, and resulting magnitude are understood.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which description matches 5/4?

visual.ariaLabel: Five fourth-size parts representing one whole and one additional fourth
visual.message: Four fourths make one whole; a fifth fourth extends beyond one whole.

choices.text: Five copies of one fourth, so the value is greater than one
choices.feedback: The denominator keeps each part at one fourth; five such parts make 5/4, which exceeds 4/4 = 1.

choices.text: Five pieces squeezed inside one whole
A fraction cannot be greater than one

hints: Ask what happens when one more fourth is counted.

screens.label: Reveal
screens.title: Fractions locate quantities, including beyond one.

visual.message: The part size stays one fourth while the count reaches five.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: Interpret 2/3 from the model.

visual.ariaLabel: A whole divided into three equal parts with two selected
visual.message: The whole has 3 equal parts and 2 are selected.

choices.text: Two copies of one third
choices.feedback: The denominator makes thirds and the numerator counts two of them.

choices.text: Two parts of any size
Two divided by an unrelated 3

hints: Use the whole bar to determine what one means.
The 3 sets equal-part size before the 2 counts parts.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Reason without the model.
screens.prompt: Two same-size containers are filled to 3/4 and 3/8. Which contains more, and why?

choices.text: 3/4, because fourth-size parts are larger than eighth-size parts when the whole is the same
choices.feedback: Both count three parts, so the larger fourth-size parts produce the larger amount.

choices.text: They are equal because both numerators are 3
3/8, because 8 is the larger denominator

hints: The containers are the same size and both count 3 parts.
Compare the size of one fourth with one eighth.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: Reconstruct the two jobs.
screens.prompt: What must you know to explain the denominator and numerator of a fraction?

choices.text: The whole, equal-part size, and number of parts counted
choices.feedback: A fraction is meaningful only relative to a whole partitioned into equal parts.

choices.text: Which digit is larger
Only how many pieces are shaded

hints: Ask what was divided and whether the pieces are equal.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Use the idea with measurement.
screens.prompt: A recipe uses 5 quarter-cup scoops of oats. Which amount is that?

choices.text: 5/4 cups: one whole cup and one additional fourth of a cup
choices.feedback: Each scoop is one fourth of a cup, and five copies of one fourth make 5/4 cups.

choices.text: 5/1 cups because there are 5 scoops
4/5 cup because the smaller number goes on top

hints: The scoop size is the unit being repeated.
Count five copies of one fourth cup.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: Which explanation preserves the meaning?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains a fraction.

choices.text: The numerator and denominator are separate whole numbers.
A fraction counts equal-size parts relative to a named whole.
Every fraction must be smaller than one.

hints: Think about why the whole must be named.

screens.title: You interpreted the whole fraction.
screens.body: You connected the whole, equal-part size, part count, and magnitude.
screens.nextRecommendation: Prototype next: percent as a rate per hundred.
